shared_components: Canonical public codecs and signature verification

inputs.config: The previous explicit public registry, budget, mechanism and route configuration.
inputs.approved_outputs: Operation-bound mechanism values, accessed at successful L1. Unused values need not be supplied for pre-L1 cancellation.
inputs.sign: Explicit ideal signing callback, role-scoped to gateway/sender/receiver. Key setup and service coins must be independent of private data. Returned signatures are verified against configured keys, object domain and exact requested payload.

output: The same PUBLIC/TICK/DELIVERY/CONFIRM observation alphabet as the previous checker, including generated signed gateway replies, delivery envelopes, terminal controls, attempts and visible receipts. ACK_LOST excludes the unobserved ACK bytes, and PACKET_LOST does not create receiver state.
input_provenance: Recorder appends each input before the associated runtime invocation. Challenge coins and attempt challenges are fixed from public request/record indices; they are not extracted from observed responses. Commands may depend on prior approved public results, as in the adaptive fixture.
failure_behavior: Unsupported commands/fields and invalid signing outputs fail the candidate with local state rollback; unexpected signing-service failures propagate, never becoming ordinary signed REJECTED. This is not a proof of the privacy of those failures.
restriction_notes: SEND represents a fresh prepare/send for the current unconfirmed final frontier, not arbitrary late copies of already-confirmed packets.
One shared monotone logical clock is used in the experiment; production sender/receiver clock skew is not modeled.
The cryptographic suite is deterministic Ed25519 with fixed synthetic service keys in comparisons. Production signing oracles are an explicit assumption, not derived from public keys.
Witness traffic, disk activity, wall-clock timing and hidden lost-ACK bytes are outside the defined observed-message alphabet.
No crash/recovery/retirement, dynamic key/credential administration or resource-exhaustion simulation is added.
Only successful operations are bounded at two; the implementation still needs proof for all allowed inputs and resource limits in any claimed deployment profile.

proof_obligations.constructive_messages: Candidate implemented and exercised; does not take observed response bytes.
proof_obligations.real_to_public_state_relation: Defined in companion note, finite evidence only; general induction remains open.
proof_obligations.ideal_resource_independence: Open deployment assumption for keys, coins, clocks, loss, storage availability and scheduling.
proof_obligations.full_distribution_and_adversaries: Open; equal conditioned transcripts are not an exhaustive mechanism-distribution comparison.
proof_obligations.independent_implementation: Open; transition rules and public codecs are shared with the checker.
